name: Maroon (X11)
lede: Maroon (X11) is a bright, purplish-red variant of the more familiar [[maroon|Maroon]], defined by the X11 window-system color list rather than by any dye or pigment history.

sections.title: Two colors sharing one name
sections.body:
Our library and Wikipedia trace this value to X11's rgb.txt, the color list shipped with the X Window System, where it sits as a separate entry from the web-standard Maroon used in CSS [1]. The two are not close: the CSS Maroon is a dark brownish red, while the X11 variant is a strong purplish red, roughly thirty units apart in hue, which the ISCC-NBS system would classify under entirely different color blocks [1][2]. Neither name is documented beyond the lists themselves, so which one is the "real" Maroon is a matter of which specification a given program follows, not a settled history [1].

In Japan, the same hue value is recorded under a traditional name, Bōtan (牡丹), meaning tree peony, an unrelated naming tradition that happens to land close to the same color [3]. This X11 red's library neighbor is [[raspberry|Raspberry]], about 6 units off, with [[carmine-red|Carmine Red]] and [[mayflower|Mayflower]] on the same purplish-red stretch of the chart [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color within six units of Maroon (X11) covers at least five per cent of the canvas in only 2 works, both from India around 1900, as photographed [4]. That scarcity, over thirty times rarer than Maroon (X11)'s expected rate for Indian paintings generally, suggests this particular bright purplish red is closer to a modern specification than to any historical pigment family [4]. It functions purely as a shadow color in both cases [4]. These remain photographs of aged, varnished canvases read as screen colors, not pigment tests [4].

questions.q: Why do CSS Maroon and X11's Maroon look so different?
choices: The two color specifications define separate, unrelated values under the same name
The X11 value is simply a typo
CSS later darkened the original X11 value
questions.answer: The two color specifications define separate, unrelated values under the same name
